## **What to Look for in the Best Payroll Processing Software**


Some payroll features are more useful than others to a small team’s payroll process. The best payroll processing software for small businesses focuses on automation, accuracy, and simplicity.


Look for these features when shopping for new payroll processing software:


### **Automated payroll tax processing software.**


Payroll tax processing software should handle tax calculations, filings, compliance, and payments automatically. For small business owners, this is one of the biggest time-savers and reduces the risk of costly mistakes.


### **Time clock and scheduling integration for payroll processing software.**


The best payroll processing software connects directly with your time tracking and scheduling tools. This ensures hours worked flow straight into payroll without manual entry.


When a shift runs late or someone swaps shifts, those changes automatically update in payroll. That means fewer errors and less time double-checking timesheets.


### **Ease of setup and everyday use in payroll processing software.**


It should be easy to set up your software for payroll processing and even easier to use. Look for payroll processing system software with guided setup, simple dashboards, and clear workflows.


If it takes weeks to configure or requires constant troubleshooting, then it’s slowing you down. You should be able to run payroll in minutes, not hours.


### **Pricing transparency: what you actually pay for payroll processing software.**


[Pricing for payroll processing software](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/payroll-services-cost) can vary widely. Some tools charge per employee, while others bundle features into tiers. The best payroll processing software is upfront about costs. You should know exactly what you’re paying and what’s included before you commit.


### **Customer support and reliability from your payroll processing software provider.**


Payroll isn’t something you can afford to “figure out later.” When something goes wrong, like a missed payment or tax issue, you need fast, reliable support from your payroll processing software provider.


Look for tools that offer responsive customer support, clear documentation, and consistent system uptime. The best payroll processing software for small business owners is dependable every time you run payroll, not just when everything goes smoothly.


Now that you know what to look for, let’s compare the[best payroll processing software for small businesses](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-payroll-software) .


## **How We Evaluated the Best Payroll Processing Software**


Every payroll processing software pick in this guide had to hold up in a real shop, not just on a feature list. Before the reviews, here’s the test we used and where our numbers come from.


### **Why we judged payroll processing software on a 10-person shop.**


Picture a[restaurant](https://www.joinhomebase.com/industry/restaurant-payroll) or[retail shop](https://www.joinhomebase.com/industry/retail-payroll) with 10 employees, running payroll for the first time. You’re the owner and the payroll department. Hours live on a time clock, a spreadsheet, or a sticky note. Someone worked a split shift, someone covered a double, and the servers earned tips. You need everyone paid right and on time, and you don’t have a week to learn new payroll processing software. That’s the shop we kept in mind for every review below.


### **In house payroll processing software: the six things we checked.**


With in house payroll processing software, you own every step, so we checked each tool against the moments that trip up first-time owners:


1. **Hours to paychecks:** Do tracked hours flow into payroll, or do you retype them every pay period?
2. **Hourly pay:** Can it handle overtime, tip pools, and more than one wage rate for the same person?
3. **Tax filing and states:** Does it file and pay your payroll taxes, and where does[multi-state payroll](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/payroll-taxes-by-state) cost extra?
4. **Real monthly cost:** What does a 10-person team pay once base fees and per-person fees are counted, and does the vendor publish the price?
5. **Setup and switching:** Is setup free, and will the vendor move your data for you?
6. **Support and integrations:** Can you reach a person when something goes wrong, and does it connect to your POS and accounting tools?


No tool wins every category, so each review calls out where it fits and where it doesn’t.


### **What 10 employees cost across payroll processing software.**


Pricing pages rarely answer the question owners ask first: what will this cost me every month? Using each vendor’s published rates, here’s what 10 paid employees comes to:


- **Patriot Basic:** about $57 a month.
- **Patriot Full Service:** about $87 a month.
- **Square Payroll:** about $95 a month.
- **Homebase, Gusto Simple, and OnPay:** about $109 a month each.
- **QuickBooks Workforce Payroll:** about $120 a month.
- **Friday Startup:** about $179 a month.
- **ADP, Paychex, and Rippling:** quote by request.


Those totals count base fees plus per-person fees. They leave out add-ons such as time tracking or HR, which raise the real bill on some tools. At $109, Homebase also includes basic scheduling and basic time tracking on its free plan, which covers up to 10 employees at one location, so the price covers getting hours to paychecks, not just the paycheck.


### **Where our payroll processing software data comes from.**


Prices, plans, and features come from each vendor’s published pricing pages and official documentation. Rates assume monthly billing. When a vendor doesn’t publish a price, as with ADP, Paychex, and Rippling, we say so instead of guessing. Plans and prices change, so confirm current details on each vendor’s site before you commit.


## **Best Payroll Processing Software for Small Businesses in 2026**


Choosing the best payroll processing software depends on your current workflows and software, team size, and how you manage your business. Below are some of the top payroll processing software small business owners can count on.


### **Homebase: best payroll processing software for hourly teams.**


Built for[hourly teams](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll/hourly-payroll) ,[Homebase](https://www.joinhomebase.com/payroll) starts payroll where your shifts start. Your schedule, time clock, and timesheets feed straight into payroll, so you approve hours instead of retyping them.


- **Ideal for:** Hourly teams that want payroll connected to scheduling and time tracking.
- **Our take:** Hourly payroll gets messy fast: split shifts, tip pools, overtime, and two wage rates for one person. Homebase calculates all of it from your real time clock hours, then files and pays your payroll taxes in all 50 states and D.C. Tax and labor-law rules update automatically to help you stay compliant. You can start free with basic scheduling and time tracking, then add payroll when you’re ready.
- **Top features:** Scheduling, time clock, timesheets, payroll, tip pooling, next-day payroll, wage garnishments, and team messaging.
- **Pricing:** Free plan with basic scheduling and time tracking (one location, up to 10 employees). Payroll is an add-on at $49/month + $6/employee paid, with unlimited payroll runs.
- **Integrations:** Point-of-sale apps including Clover, Toast, and Square, plus[QuickBooks Online Plus](https://www.joinhomebase.com/integrations/quickbooks) for accounting.
- **Pros:** Scheduling, time tracking, and payroll in one app,[free setup and data transfer](https://www.joinhomebase.com/switch-payroll) , and live support from 7am to 7pm CT.
- **Cons:** Built for hourly teams, so Homebase is a weaker fit for salaried-only teams or large businesses. Payroll is a paid add-on.


### **Friday App: best payroll processing software for simple, flat pricing.**


[Friday](https://fridayapp.com/) keeps payroll simple: pick a plan, pay a base fee plus a per-user price, and get payroll with time tracking built in.


- **Ideal for:** Small teams that want payroll and time tracking in one tool, with published pricing.
- **Our take:** The Startup plan covers unlimited payrolls, tax filing and compliance, W-2s and 1099s, direct deposit, and autopay. Multi-state payroll, PTO accrual policies, and next-day payroll (subject to bank approval) come with Small Biz Pro, so check which plan matches your team before you commit.
- **Top features:** Time tracking with geofencing, unlimited payrolls, tax filing and compliance, W-2s and 1099s, direct deposit, printable checks, and autopay.
- **Pricing:** Startup is $59/month base + $12/user. Small Biz Pro is $99/month base + $16/user. A time-tracking-only plan is $9/user with no base fee.
- **Integrations:** QuickBooks integrations.
- **Pros:** Published pricing, time tracking on every plan, and payroll tax filing included.
- **Cons:** Multi-state payroll and next-day payroll need the higher-priced Small Biz Pro plan. The per-user fee adds up as your team grows.


### **Patriot Software: best payroll processing software for low-cost payroll.**


[Patriot](https://www.patriotsoftware.com/) is one of the lowest-priced ways to run payroll, and a good match for owners comfortable handling some tax tasks themselves.


- **Ideal for:** Budget-minded teams that want a low entry price and don’t mind a more hands-on setup.
- **Our take:** Basic Payroll covers payroll calculations, direct deposit, and unlimited payroll runs, but you file your own taxes. Full Service Payroll has Patriot file and pay your payroll taxes for you, so price that plan out if you don’t want to handle filings.
- **Top features:** Basic and Full Service payroll, direct deposit, an employee portal, unlimited payroll runs, and optional tax filing.
- **Pricing:** Basic Payroll is $17/month + $4/worker paid. Full Service Payroll is $37/month + $5/worker paid. Time and attendance and HR add-ons are $6/month + $2/employee each, and accounting software is a separate monthly cost.
- **Integrations:** Patriot also sells accounting software and time and attendance as separate add-ons.
- **Pros:** Low entry price, unlimited payroll runs, and free direct deposit and employee portal.
- **Cons:** Full Service includes one state, and each extra state costs $12/month. Time tracking and HR cost extra.
- **Head-to-head:** See the full[Homebase vs. Patriot comparison](https://www.joinhomebase.com/compare/homebase-vs-patriot) .


### **Gusto: best payroll processing software for built-in HR and benefits.**


[Gusto](https://gusto.com/) pairs payroll with PTO policies, benefits, and HR tools, which makes it a strong fit when HR is as big a job as payroll.


- **Ideal for:** Teams that want payroll, HR tools, and benefits in one app.
- **Our take:** Simple covers single-state payroll with unlimited payroll runs and tax filings. Multi-state payroll, next-day pay, and time tracking start at Plus, and the price climbs with each tier.
- **Top features:** Unlimited payroll runs, tax filings and payments, PTO policies, health benefits, and HR tools.
- **Pricing:** Simple is $49/month + $6/person. Plus is $80/month + $12/person. Premium is $180/month + $22/person.
- **Integrations:** QuickBooks, Xero, FreshBooks, Expensify, Hubstaff, Clover, and[Homebase](https://www.joinhomebase.com/integrations/gusto) .
- **Pros:** Published pricing, unlimited payroll runs on every plan, and a broad benefits lineup.
- **Cons:** Simple covers one state only. Next-day pay, priority support, and HR resources cost extra or need a higher plan.
- **Head-to-head:** See the full[Homebase vs. Gusto comparison](https://www.joinhomebase.com/compare/homebase-vs-gusto) .


### **QuickBooks Workforce (formerly QuickBooks Payroll): best payroll processing software for QuickBooks users.**


If your books already live in[QuickBooks](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/) , payroll that sits right beside them keeps your accounting and paychecks in sync.


- **Ideal for:** Businesses already running their accounting in QuickBooks.
- **Our take:** Workforce Payroll covers full-service payroll with tax filing and next-day direct deposit. Premium and Elite add time tracking, hiring and onboarding, and same-day direct deposit.
- **Top features:** Full-service payroll, auto payroll for salaried employees, 1099 e-file, direct deposit, and an employee portal.
- **Pricing:** Workforce Payroll is $50/month + $7/employee. Premium is $88/month + $13/employee. Elite is $134/month + $17/employee.
- **Integrations:** QuickBooks accounting, plus health benefits through Allstate, 401(k) plans through Vestwell, workers’ comp through NEXT (not available in OH, ND, WA, and WY), and background checks through Checkr.
- **Pros:** Fits QuickBooks accounting, same-day direct deposit on Premium and Elite, and benefits available through partners.
- **Cons:** Time tracking needs Premium or higher, and the per-employee price rises with each tier.
- **Head-to-head:** See the full[Homebase vs. QuickBooks comparison](https://www.joinhomebase.com/compare/homebase-vs-quickbooks) .


### **ADP RUN: best payroll processing software for expert support.**


[ADP RUN](https://www.adp.com/) is built for small businesses and comes in four packages that add HR help as you move up.


- **Ideal for:** Growing teams that want expert payroll support and room to add HR help.
- **Our take:** ADP offers 24/7 real-person payroll support and does the tax filing for you. ADP doesn’t publish RUN pricing, so you’ll need a quote to compare costs.
- **Top features:** Full-service payroll with tax filing, employee access and onboarding, reporting, and four packages: Essential, Enhanced, Complete, and HR Pro.
- **Pricing:** Quote only. ADP doesn’t publish RUN pricing.
- **Integrations:** Enhanced adds ZipRecruiter job posting.
- **Pros:** 24/7 payroll support, four packages to grow into, and HR help on higher tiers.
- **Cons:** No published pricing, so comparing costs takes a sales conversation. Higher tiers add HR features you may not need.
- **Head-to-head:** See the full[Homebase vs. ADP comparison](https://www.joinhomebase.com/compare/homebase-vs-adp) .


### **Paychex Flex: best payroll processing software for full-service payroll with add-ons.**


[Paychex Flex](https://www.paychex.com/) layers HR, time and attendance, hiring, and benefits services on top of full-service payroll.


- **Ideal for:** Teams that want full-service payroll with optional HR, time, and benefits services.
- **Our take:** Paychex automates payroll tax calculation, payment, and filing. Pricing is by quote.
- **Top features:** Payroll with tax administration, direct deposit, reporting, a mobile app, new hire reporting, and 24/7 support.
- **Pricing:** Quote only. Paychex shows a request-pricing button instead of a published price.
- **Integrations:** Time and attendance, HR, hiring, and benefits services in the same Paychex account.
- **Pros:** Payroll tax administration, 24/7 support, and HR and time and attendance services in the same account.
- **Cons:** No published pricing, so you’ll need a quote to compare costs.


### **Rippling: best payroll processing software for HR, IT, and payroll in one system.**


[Rippling](https://www.rippling.com/) starts with an HR system and adds payroll, benefits, and device and app management as separate modules.


- **Ideal for:** Teams that want HR, IT, and payroll managed in one system.
- **Our take:** That layered setup is a strong fit when onboarding a new hire means payroll setup and laptop access at the same time. It also means the total grows with each module you add.
- **Top features:** HR records, US payroll, and IT management.
- **Pricing:** Quote-based. The core system starts at $8/user plus a monthly base fee, and payroll is added on top.
- **Integrations:** 650+ app integrations.
- **Pros:** HR, IT, and payroll in one system, and a large integration library.
- **Cons:** Payroll is an add-on to the required core system, so cost builds with each module. Pricing needs a quote.


### **OnPay: best payroll processing software for flat, multi-state pricing.**


[OnPay](https://onpay.com/) keeps pricing simple: one base fee plus a per-worker fee, with unlimited pay runs and multi-state payroll included.


- **Ideal for:** Businesses that want one flat price and multi-state payroll without extra fees.
- **Our take:** OnPay files federal, state, and local taxes and offers free setup and data migration, so switching from another provider doesn’t add a one-time bill.
- **Top features:** Full-service payroll for W-2 and 1099 workers, federal, state, and local tax filings, unlimited pay runs, and hiring and onboarding.
- **Pricing:** $49/month base + $6/worker. The HR add-on is $15/month + $2/worker.
- **Integrations:** Accounting and time tracking apps.
- **Pros:** Flat pricing, multi-state payroll included, free setup and data migration, and support by phone, chat, and email.
- **Cons:** Time tracking connects through integrations. HR features such as PTO management cost extra.


### **Square Payroll: best payroll processing software for Square POS users.**


[Square Payroll](https://squareup.com/) fits teams that already run their business on Square.


- **Ideal for:** Businesses already using Square POS.
- **Our take:** It’s full-service payroll with unlimited pay runs and tax filing, and you can pay by check, direct deposit, or Cash App. Contractor-only payroll has no base fee.
- **Top features:** Unlimited pay runs, tax filing, direct deposit, and contractor payments.
- **Pricing:** Full-service payroll is $35/month + $6/person paid. Contractor-only payroll is $6/person paid per month with no base fee.
- **Integrations:** Works together with Square Staff tools, plus easy payroll integration across the Square ecosystem.
- **Pros:** A $35 base fee, lower than most tools here, plus a natural fit with the Square ecosystem.
- **Cons:** Works best inside Square, and Forbes notes[it may not scale well](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/business/square-payroll-review/) for larger teams.
- **Head-to-head:** See the full[Homebase vs. Square comparison](https://www.joinhomebase.com/compare/homebase-vs-square) .


## **Free Payroll Processing Software: What’s Actually Free and What Isn’t**


With so many options available, you may be wondering if you can just start with[free payroll processing software](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/free-payroll-software-for-small-business) instead. Free payroll processing software can be appealing, especially when you’re just starting out. But “free” often comes with limitations.


### **What free payroll processing software typically includes.**


Free payroll processing software usually includes basic payroll calculations and limited employee management. Some tools offer free tiers with optional paid add-ons for tax filing or direct deposit.


These plans can work for[small teams or businesses with simple payroll needs](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-do-payroll-for-small-business) . But they often require more manual work and oversight.


So, if you’re considering a free option, think about whether the functionalities you get outweigh the limitations. If they don’t, then maybe a paid option would be better.


### **When it makes sense to pay for payroll processing software.**


Paying for payroll processing software makes sense when you want features that aren’t included in the free plan, like payroll automation and compliance support. Automated tax filing and integrated time tracking can quickly justify the cost, especially with the time you’ll save.


As your team grows, manual payroll management becomes harder. Investing in the right payroll processing software helps you scale without adding complexity.


### **Risks of relying on free payroll processing software.**


Free payroll processing software can work in the short term, but it often comes with trade-offs. Limited automation, manual tax handling, and fewer integrations can increase your workload and risk of errors.


As your team grows, those limitations start to show. What saved you money upfront can end up costing more in time, mistakes, or compliance issues, especially without built-in payroll tax processing software.


Once you narrow down your options, it’s worth taking a closer look at how specific tools can fit your workflow, whether they’re free or paid.


## **Is Homebase the Right Payroll Processing Software for Your Business?**


Homebase is a strong option for businesses managing hourly employees. But like any payroll processing software, Homebase works best in specific situations.


### **Where Homebase works best as payroll processing software.**


[Homebase payroll](https://app.joinhomebase.com/onboarding/sign-up) works best for restaurants, retail stores, salons, and service businesses. These teams often deal with shift changes, hourly wages, and last-minute scheduling chaos.


Because[scheduling](https://www.joinhomebase.com/employee-scheduling) ,[time tracking](https://www.joinhomebase.com/time-clock/time-tracking) , and payroll are all connected in Homebase, you avoid manual data entry. This makes Homebase one of the best software for easy payroll processing for hourly teams.


### **Where another payroll processing software is a better fit.**


Another payroll processing software might be better if your team is fully salaried or needs deep accounting integrations. Tools like QuickBooks Workforce or Gusto may offer more flexibility in those cases.


If your business has complex benefits or multi-state compliance needs, then you may still need a more advanced payroll tax processing software. Or, if your payroll process is especially complex, you may even consider outsourcing your payroll.


Before you invest in a new payroll processing software, here are some steps that will help you choose the best fit.


## **How to Choose the Right Payroll Processing Software for Your Business**


Choosing the right payroll processing software comes down to how your business actually runs. The goal is to find payroll processing software that fits your workflow, team, and budget.


### **Match payroll processing software to your team type: hourly or salaried.**


Your team structure has a big impact on what payroll processing software you need.


Hourly teams require time tracking, scheduling integration, and shift-based payroll, while salaried teams are usually more straightforward. This also affects your total payroll costs and how you’ll budget for new software.


If you manage hourly workers, look for payroll processing software that connects scheduling and payroll. This reduces manual work and helps ensure employees are paid accurately for every hour worked.


### **Map your workflow before you choose payroll processing software.**


Before choosing software for payroll processing, take a step back and look at your current payroll process. Where are you spending the most time? Where do mistakes or delays happen?


Common pain points include manual data entry, disconnected systems, and last-minute changes from time tracking. Identifying these gaps helps you choose payroll processing software that solves your problems.


### **Prioritize must-have features in payroll processing software.**


It’s easy to get distracted by extra features, but not all of them matter for your business. Focus first on must-haves like automated payroll tax processing, direct deposit, and accurate time tracking.


Nice-to-haves like advanced payroll reporting or HR tools can be helpful, but only if you’ll actually use them. The best payroll processing software keeps things simple while covering your core needs.


### **Choose scalable payroll processing software for where you’re headed.**


Your payroll needs today might not match your needs six months from now. If you’re planning to hire more employees or expand locations, your payroll processing software should be able to grow with you.


Choosing scalable payroll processing software for small business helps you avoid switching payroll tools later. It also ensures your systems stay consistent as your team grows.


### **Compare payroll processing software against your needs and budget.**


Once you understand your workflow, team type, and priorities, it’s easier to compare options. Look at pricing, features, ease of use, and how well each tool fits your day-to-day operations.


The right payroll processing software is the one that saves you time, reduces payroll errors, and fits your budget. Keep your decision practical, and choose the tool your team will actually use.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Payroll Processing Software**


### **What is the best payroll processing software?**


The best payroll processing software is the one that matches how your team works, and for hourly teams that means payroll connected to scheduling and time tracking. Homebase does that in one app, Gusto fits teams that want built-in HR and benefits, and QuickBooks Workforce fits businesses already on QuickBooks.


### **What is the best payroll processing software for small business?**


The best payroll processing software for small business combines full-service tax filing with simple setup and transparent pricing. For hourly teams, Homebase adds basic scheduling and time tracking on a free plan, with payroll at $49 a month plus $6 per employee paid.


### **What is payroll processing software?**


Payroll processing software calculates wages, withholds and files payroll taxes, and pays your team by direct deposit or check. It replaces spreadsheets and manual math with automated calculations, so every pay run is faster, more accurate, and easier to repeat.


### **How does payroll processing software work?**


Payroll processing software takes the hours your team worked, calculates gross pay, deductions, and taxes, and then pays your team and files your payroll taxes. When your time clock feeds payroll directly, as it does in Homebase, hours flow in without retyping.


### **How much does payroll processing software cost?**


Payroll processing software for small businesses typically costs a monthly base fee plus a per-employee fee, with published rates in this guide running from $17 to $59 a month plus $4 to $12 per person. ADP, Paychex, and Rippling quote by request.


### **What is the cheapest payroll processing software?**


The cheapest payroll processing software for employee payroll in this guide is Patriot Software, at $17 a month plus $4 per worker for Basic Payroll, where you file your own taxes. Full Service Payroll, where Patriot files taxes for you, costs $37 a month plus $5 per worker.


### **What is the best payroll processing software for restaurants?**


The best[payroll processing software for restaurants](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/payroll-software-for-restaurants) calculates tip pools, multiple wage rates, and overtime from your real time clock hours. Built for hourly teams, Homebase handles tip pooling, multiple wage rates, and payroll that runs straight from your scheduling and timesheets.


### **What payroll processing software supports hourly workers?**


Payroll processing software that supports hourly workers calculates pay from tracked hours, including overtime, breaks, and multiple wage rates. Both Homebase and Friday App connect time tracking to payroll, and Homebase adds scheduling in the same app so your schedule and your paychecks stay in sync.


### **Is there free payroll processing software?**


Free payroll processing software is uncommon, because full-service payroll with tax filing is usually a paid add-on. Homebase has a free plan for basic scheduling and time tracking, and you add payroll at $49 a month plus $6 per employee paid when you’re ready.


### **Do I need payroll processing software for one employee?**


Payroll processing software is worth using even for one employee, because it calculates, files, and pays your payroll taxes for you. With one worker, base fees dominate: Gusto Simple runs $55 a month and Square Payroll runs $41 a month.


### **Is ADP or QuickBooks better payroll processing software?**


ADP RUN suits growing teams that want hands-on payroll support, while QuickBooks Workforce suits businesses already running their books in QuickBooks. ADP doesn’t publish RUN pricing, so you’ll need a quote, and QuickBooks Workforce Payroll starts at $50 a month plus $7 per employee.


### **Can ChatGPT replace payroll processing software?**


ChatGPT can explain payroll concepts, help you compare tools, and draft policies, but it can’t replace payroll processing software. Payroll needs secure systems that calculate wages, file taxes, and move money to your team, and a chatbot does none of that.
